hints: Use the fact that the larger intercept $b$ is an integer root of the polynomial.
Test plausible integer factors of the constant term $-6$ in $x^4-2x^3-7x-6$ and identify the positive root shown on the right of the diagram.
walkthrough:
The $x$-intercept $b$ is a positive integer root of the equation $y = 0$:
$$x^4 - 2x^3 - 7x - 6 = 0$$

hints: Use the factor theorem with the integer root $b$ from part (i).
Divide $x^4-2x^3-7x-6$ by $x-b$ to obtain the cubic factor whose other real root is $a$.
Set the cubic factor equal to zero at $x=a$, then isolate the linear $3a$ term to make $a$ the subject.
walkthrough: Since $b = 3$ is a root, $(x - 3)$ is a linear factor of $x^4 - 2x^3 - 7x - 6$.

Perform polynomial division of $(x^4 - 2x^3 - 7x - 6)$ by $(x - 3)$:
- Divide $x^4$ by $x$: quotient term $x^3$.
  Multiply: $x^3(x - 3) = x^4 - 3x^3$.
  Subtract: $(-2x^3) - (-3x^3) = x^3$.
- Divide $x^3$ by $x$: quotient term $x^2$.
  Multiply: $x^2(x - 3) = x^3 - 3x^2$.
  Subtract: $(0x^2) - (-3x^2) = 3x^2$.
- Divide $3x^2$ by $x$: quotient term $3x$.
  Multiply: $3x(x - 3) = 3x^2 - 9x$.
  Subtract: $(-7x) - (-9x) = 2x$.
- Divide $2x$ by $x$: quotient term $2$.
  Multiply: $2(x - 3) = 2x - 6$.
  Subtract: $(-6) - (-6) = 0$.

Since $a$ is the other real $x$-intercept ($a < 3$), $a$ must be a root of the cubic quotient:
$$a^3 + a^2 + 3a + 2 = 0$$

Rearrange to make $a$ the subject:
$$3a = -(2 + a^2 + a^3)$$
$$a = -\dfrac{1}{3}(2 + a^2 + a^3)$$
This completes the proof.

hints: Use the fixed-point rearrangement from part (ii) as $a_{n+1}=-\tfrac13(2+a_n^2+a_n^3)$.
Start with a reasonable negative value near the left intercept and report each iterate to 5 decimal places.
Continue until the iterates agree sufficiently to justify a stable value to 3 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Write the iterative formula based on part (ii):
$$a_{n+1} = -\dfrac{1}{3}\bigl(2 + a_n^2 + a_n^3\bigr)$$

Observe that the sequence has converged to 5 decimal places at $-0.71523$.
Round to 3 decimal places:
$$a \approx -0.715$$
